parts.name: tilapia
sources: World: a smooth skin around the bones of World (World.Blob), fins and eyes (scripts/fish_template.exs). AGPL-3.0, as World
A Nile tilapia (cá rô phi, Oreochromis niloticus): about 30 cm long, a deep body, gray with a darker back and a pale belly, a gray dorsal fin.

Wikipedia, Nile tilapia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nile_tilapia): "The Nile tilapia reaches up to 60 cm (24 in) in length"; "Wild, natural-type Nile tilapias are brownish or grayish overall, often with indistinct banding on their body"; "the tail is vertically striped"; the edge of the dorsal fin "is gray or black in Nile tilapia".

The length (30 cm, a fish of a farm pond), the deep body (body_depth 1.4) and the colors: a guess from photos of iNaturalist: https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/494958758, https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/444066694. The tail fin of the template is forked; the tail fin of a tilapia is not. No bands: the coat has no region for them.
